summary:

positions.commentary: Amazon's influence on brick-and-mortar retailers was a key factor in the firm's deep value investment thesis regarding Abercrombie and Fitch.
The firm believes the loss of the Costco account would unlock capital for American Express to repurchase shares, driving EPS growth.
Costco could demand better terms from American Express, leading Amex to walk away from the business as a strength.

thesis: This episode argues that Amazon's disruption of brick-and-mortar retail created specific deep value opportunities, notably in Abercrombie and Fitch. It also posits that American Express possesses a robust business model with natural inflation protection and that the loss of the Costco account may ultimately unlock capital for share repurchases to drive EPS growth.

claims.claim: Amazon's influence on brick-and-mortar retailers created investment opportunities for the firm in various areas.
claims.quote: So, for instance, Amazon.com has had a clear influence on retail across the world, really, but across the country, big time. Brick-and-mortar retailers under severe pressure because of online presence, not just from people moving online, but retailers having to invest in online capabilities, which has hurt their profitability.

claims.claim: Amazon's influence on brick-and-mortar retailers was a key factor in the firm's deep value investment thesis regarding Abercrombie and Fitch.
claims.quote: And then the valuation, again, because of Amazon.com's influence on the brick-and-mortar retailers, Abercrombie and Fitch was trading, in our opinion, well below what even Hollister was worth.

claims.claim: American Express has a fantastic business model, keeps all the economics of their cards, and offers natural inflation protection.
claims.quote: Amex has a fantastic business model. They keep all the economics of their cards, which is rare. And also inflation protection, which is a big deal in today's environment. wasn't a big deal when we purchased it, but we were getting inflation protection for free because essentially American Express's revenue, they get a percentage of every charge.

claims.claim: The firm believes the loss of the Costco account would unlock capital for American Express to repurchase shares, driving EPS growth.

claims.claim: American Express lost the Costco account several years ago, causing people to worry about Amex's competitive edge and brand power.
claims.quote: So you can think, as an example, American Express, when they lost the Costco account. Several years ago, people were worried maybe Amex is losing its competitive edge. its brand power is not strong enough to keep Costco.

claims.claim: Costco could demand better terms from American Express, leading Amex to walk away from the business as a strength.
claims.quote: Costco had grown, obviously could demand better terms, and Amex said we won't play with those terms. They walked away from the business.

numbers.what: percentage of GameStop stores that could be shut down while remaining cash flow positive
numbers.quote: So at the time we initiated our position in GameStop, we believe that about 20 to 25 percent of their stores could be shut down and it would be cash flow positive to the overall company.

numbers.what: average holding period of the typical investor
numbers.quote: I can't remember at this point who said, oh yeah, this investor, they're a very long. term investor. They have about a one-year holding period on average.

numbers.what: investment time frame for deep value companies
numbers.quote: We're looking three to five years into the future, even for our deep value companies, and these are opportunistic.
But our turnover historically has been quite low three to five year investment time frame and about 30% average turnover, even a little bit lower than that for the first decade plus.

numbers.what: percentage of Abercrombie and Fitch stores quietly shut down
numbers.quote: They had quietly shut down 25% of those stores.

numbers.what: percentage of Abercrombie and Fitch sales through e-commerce
numbers.quote: Twenty-five percent of their sales were through e-commerce.

numbers.what: timeframe for e-commerce sales to overtake revenue decline at Abercrombie and Fitch
numbers.quote: E-commerce sales would overtake the decline within 18 to 24 months.

numbers.what: percentage drop in Abercrombie and Fitch stock price in worst case scenario
numbers.quote: We applied a price to sales multiple of the lowest going concern retailers in the market to Hollister alone, ignoring Abercrombian Fitch, the namesake brand, and thought that the stock could only drop maybe about 20% more.

numbers.what: reward to risk ratio for Abercrombie and Fitch investment
numbers.quote: So more than 100% upside versus 20% downside gives us a 5 to 1 reward to risk ratio, which highlights how we think about the world.

numbers.what: percentage of portfolio allocated to core value side
numbers.quote: The core value side is, again, the larger part of our portfolios, 50 to 75%.

numbers.what: number of companies on all-cap strategy watch list
numbers.quote: About 135 companies for our all-cap strategy, about 100 small caps that we believe are the best companies that trade in the U.S. stock market.
